analysis.title: Americas Transportation: Valuation Tracker: Transports Outperformance Led By Parcels and Rails in October
key_insights: Transport stocks were mixed against the S&P 500 in October. 16 of the 25 covered names outperformed and 9 underperformed. The 25 names averaged +4% versus the S&P 500 at -1% and the S&P Equal-Weight Index at +5%.
Parcels led the subsectors in October at +13% (UPS +16%, FDX +10%). Rails returned +9% (CSX +12%) and Railcar Lessors/Manufacturers +6% (TRN +15%).
Trucking was the weakest subsector in October. Truckload (TL) fell 10% (WERN -18.5%, SNDR -8%, KNX -4%) and LTL was flat (FDXF +15%, TFII -22%). Logistics gained 2% (RXO +34%, CHRW -16%).

Year to date through October, Logistics and Rails are each up 28% (Logistics ex-RXO +6%), Parcels +22%, Trucking +13% (TL +6%, LTL +19%) and Railcar Lessors/Manufacturers +1%, against the S&P 500 at +11%.
Best October performers in coverage were RXO (+34%), R (+24%) and UPS (+16%). Worst were TFII (-22%), WERN (-18%) and CHRW (-16%).
Best YTD performers through October are RXO (+118%), ARCB (+69%) and R (+47%). Worst are CHRW (-22%), GBX (-17%) and TFII (-10%).
Parcels trade at 14.4x P/E at end of October, above the 5-year average of 13.7x and up from 13x at end of September.

Rails trade at an average 21.9x P/E versus 20.9x at end of September and a ~19.7x 5-year average, about a 14% premium to the S&P 500. US railroads trade above their 5-year averages while Canadian rails trade below theirs.
Logistics trades at 21.2x P/E, below its 22.1x 5-year average. GS suggests the legal overhang on CHRW may be a factor. CHRW is at 17.2x, down from ~22x at end of September and ~28x in July.
LTL trades at 23.4x P/E, close to its 5-year average and well below the +1SD level of 28.7x. The multiple has compressed ~8 turns since end of June.

Truckload trades at 16.9x P/E, down ~11 turns since end of June and below the ~19.4x historical average. The market has turned negative on driver and fuel related headwinds that companies called out in 3Q despite still strong rates.
Railcar Lessors/Manufacturers trade at 13.6x P/E, one turn higher than end of September and above the group's -1SD level of ~13.3x.

GS keeps its June 2025 ratings rotation. Buy on trucking (ODFL, SAIA, ARCB, WERN, SNDR, KNX) and Neutral on rails and rail-related names (CSX, UNP, CP, JBHT). GS positions for the early-cycle TL and LTL names because a freight bottom could give more earnings leverage as density fills in and pricing steps up.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees the truck cycle showing many traditional signs of bottoming before an inflection and sees upside to Trucking shares. It holds Buy ratings on ODFL, SAIA, ARCB, WERN, SNDR and KNX.
GS downgraded CSX, UNP, CP and JBHT to Neutral in June 2025. US railroads trade above 5-year average P/E multiples.

earnings_insights: Companies called out driver and fuel related headwinds in 3Q results while freight rates stayed strong, per GS. The report links these to the truckload multiple falling to 16.9x P/E at end of October.
